A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LoRA-MCL research work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v2 reports original Markov-chain simulations, audio and image captioning experiments, bilingual specialization analyses, and machine translation results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds training-cost measurements and a three-hypothesis bilingual specialization experiment.

M1.justification: The multiple LoRA adapters, winner-takes-all objectives, relaxed and annealed variants, and grouped-convolution implementation are already present in v2. v3 evaluates existing components without changing the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use Markov mixtures, AudioCaps, Clotho-V2, TextCaps including its English/French variant, and English–German translation data. The added cost measurements reuse existing coverage; increasing the bilingual model's hypothesis count changes its configuration.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparison methods remain LoRA-MLE, LoRA-MoE with its decoding variants, multi-head MCL, DAC-RLD, and PaliGemma-3B. The added rank-40 loss row uses an existing LoRA-MLE configuration, while standard versus grouped implementation comparisons analyze variants of the proposed method.

E3.justification: v3 adds training-time and peak-memory evaluation across hypothesis counts, measuring audio training over 100 iterations. The additional bilingual experiment uses K=3 and per-reference BLEU-4 winning rates; the original K=2 experiment and its SPIDEr-based winner assessment remain. Existing benchmark splits and training recipes are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix E.5 adds cost comparisons of standard and grouped implementations on the synthetic and audio setups. Appendix E.7.4 extends the existing bilingual specialization analysis to K=3, testing behavior when hypotheses outnumber language modes. Earlier relaxation, multi-head initialization, and SVM specialization analyses remain.

E5.justification: The three-seed mean and standard-deviation reporting for synthetic loss curves is retained. New Tables 5–7 disclose averaging cost measurements over ten seeds for the toy setup and five seeds for each audio setup, with timing values reported using ± variation. These counts concern new experiments.

E6.justification: v3 adds cost results and K=3 winning rates, including 67% of French references won by hypothesis 3. Table 1 adds rank-40 LoRA-MLE losses of 2.181 on AudioCaps and 2.910 on Clotho. Several Clotho LoRA-MoE values change: for example, beam-search width 25 SPIDEr changes from 0.405 to 0.411 in v2 Table 8 versus v3 Table 11, also reflected in Figure 3. Main LoRA-MCL quality scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The propositions, corollaries, assumptions, bounds, and proofs in Section 4 and Appendices A–C are retained. The LoRA-MoE expression's replacement of the frozen-layer function by hW and other notation edits do not establish changed mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: adapting MCL through LoRA, capturing mixture modes, and producing diverse, plausible outputs across captioning and translation. The new diagnostics do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix E.5 qualifies the acceleration discussion with measured memory overhead and cases where grouped computation is slower on Clotho. It attributes the slowdown to non-contiguous memory layouts from reshaping and suggests custom kernels. The conclusion also adds pretraining as a future direction.

D1.justification: The new cost tables specify benchmark hardware, including a Tesla P100-16GB for the toy setup and an H100-80GB for audio. Section 5.2 explicitly identifies Figure 3's DBS penalty as 1.0, and Appendix E.6.2 changes the recommended relaxation range from [0,0.1] to (0,0.1]. Table 3's expanded rank/scaling caption repeats details already supplied in v2 Table 12.

R1.justification: v3 adds Dempster et al. (1977) to support the existing EM connection. Other changes largely update publication metadata, including the Makkuva and Kaya references; the substantive positioning relative to MCL, MoE, and diverse generation remains stable.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized grammar, terminology, and heading corrections, adds explanatory paragraph headings, and introduces impact and acknowledgment sections with conference publication information. The overall section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds cost Tables 5–7 and a four-panel PCA visualization with winning-rate Table 16. Table 1 gains a row, Table 3 receives an expanded caption, and existing main-text figures, tables, and appendix examples are relocated through reflow. The established visual format is retained.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens v2's implementation discussion with measured runtime and memory trade-offs, including transparent reporting of the Clotho slowdown in Tables 5–7. Figure 8 and Table 16 also extend evidence about specialization beyond two hypotheses. These targeted additions improve empirical support and practical clarity while leaving the core method, theory, and principal quality results largely unchanged.
